land.text: 'Thessalonica and its environs' and 'the dynasty's lands in Thessaly' left to Manuel Komnenos Doukas after Theodore's defeat at Klokotnitsa (1230)

predecessors.note: The Empire page's infobox gives 'Epirus conquest of Thessalonika: 1224' and 'Predecessor: Despotate of Epirus / Kingdom of Thessalonica'. The despotate-of-epirus dossier carries Theodore's 1224-1230 state (styled Empire of Thessalonica from 1225/1227) and records the 1230 split; this dossier starts at the split, as the Manuel Komnenos Doukas page does (rule at Thessalonica from 1230).

land.text: 'Thessalonica was incorporated into the Nicaean state' under the governor Andronikos Palaiologos (1246)

successors.note: Cliopatria draws the 1241 shape to 1249; the Nicaean Empire row does not take over Thessalonica until after that.

capitals.name: Thessalonica (Thessaloniki)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Thessalonica'. Theodore retired to Vodena after his release in 1237 and was exiled there after 1246 (rulers table), but remained 'the actual power behind the throne'.

rulers.name: Manuel Komnenos Doukas
rulers.title: despot (despotes)
rulers.note: Ruled at Thessalonica and its environs with the title of despotes by leave of Ivan Asen II; deposed in 1237 (the Empire page calls it Theodore's coup; the Manuel page says Theodore and his sons were released and Manuel 'was forced to flee to Asia Minor').

rulers.name: John Komnenos Doukas
rulers.title: emperor 1237-1242, then despot
rulers.note: Crowned by his father Theodore, who remained the real power; in 1242 he renounced the imperial title and accepted Nicaean authority as Despot.

rulers.name: Demetrios Angelos Doukas
rulers.title: despot
rulers.note: Succeeded his brother John in 1244; unpopular; exiled to Asia Minor after the Nicaean takeover in 1246.

correction.text: Thessalonica and its environs and the dynasty's lands in Thessaly, as Cliopatria draws them from 1236

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1230-1235: Cliopatria's row begins in 1236 but the state begins in 1230, when 'Manuel was allowed by Ivan Asen II to rule in Thessalonica and its environs with the title of despotes' (Manuel page). The Empire page says he kept 'Thessalonica's environs and the dynasty's lands in Thessaly and Epirus'; the Manuel page names only Thessalonica and its environs until he took Larissa and Pharsalos in 1239. The 1236 shape (Thessalonica plus Thessaly, 22,045 km2) is used on the state's own page; the pages conflict on whether Thessaly was Manuel's before 1237 (see notes). Epirus proper went to Michael II.

Years only: 22,045 km2 holds 1236-1238. In 1239 Manuel Komnenos Doukas takes Larissa and Pharsalos from John, so Thessaly goes (see empire-of-thessalonica_1239); Cliopatria keeps it to 1240. The Empire page gives no area for either date; the shape (Thessalonica plus Thessaly, bbox 21.36-24.81 E, 38.87-40.94 N) is in line with the lands the page names.

correction.text: Thessalonica and its environs without the Thessalian fortresses (Larissa, Pharsalos) taken by Manuel in 1239

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1239-1240: 'He returned to Greece in 1239 with Nicaean support and captured several fortresses, including Larissa and Pharsalos, from Theodore's son John Komnenos Doukas', ruling Thessaly until about 1241 (Manuel page; the Empire page: 'ruled Thessaly until his death in 1241'). Cliopatria keeps Thessaly in the Empire's row to 1240 and drops it in 1241; the correction drops it from 1239. Thessaly's region name is my reading of 'several fortresses, including Larissa and Pharsalos'.

correction.text: shape unchanged; holds 1241-1246 only; the years 1247-1249 are Nicaean

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 7,594 km2 (Thessalonica and its environs, bbox 22.10-24.81 E, 40.22-40.94 N) holds 1241-1246. After Manuel's death 'it [Thessaly] was quickly occupied by Michael II of Epirus', which is why Thessaly is absent. Cliopatria runs the row to 1249, but 'Thessalonica was incorporated into the Nicaean state' in 1246, so 1247-1249 belong to the Nicaean Empire.

region.text: Thessalonica and its environs, with the dynasty's lands in Thessaly

ledger.note: 1230: after Klokotnitsa Manuel Komnenos Doukas rules the Thessalonican remnant under Bulgarian leave. Theodore's army was destroyed and he 'was captured and later blinded'; Bulgaria took most of Theodore's Thracian lands and most of Macedonia and Albania; Manuel 'became forced to acknowledge himself Asen's vassal', keeping 'Thessalonica's environs and the dynasty's lands in Thessaly and Epirus', while 'Epirus broke away under Michael II' (infobox: vassal of Bulgaria 1230-37). The page gives the years, the extent is the researcher's reading; the Manuel page names only Thessalonica and its environs.

1237: Theodore returns to power through his son John. 'Theodore deposed Manuel in a coup in 1237' and 'crowned his son John, remaining the actual power behind the throne' (Empire page); the Manuel page: Theodore and his sons were released and Manuel 'was forced to flee to Asia Minor'. The state continues under John Komnenos Doukas as emperor.

region.text: Larissa, Pharsalos and several other Thessalian fortresses

ledger.note: 1239: Manuel Komnenos Doukas takes Larissa and Pharsalos. 'He returned to Greece in 1239 with Nicaean support and captured several fortresses, including Larissa and Pharsalos, from Theodore's son John Komnenos Doukas', and ruled Thessaly until about 1241; 'it was quickly occupied by Michael II of Epirus' afterwards (Empire page). Cliopatria and the despotate-of-epirus dossier give the Thessaly hand-over in 1241.

1242: John Komnenos Doukas gives up the imperial title and accepts Nicaean authority. 'In 1242, John renounced the imperial title and accepted Nicaean authority in exchange for remaining ruler as Despot' (infobox: Nicaean suzerainty 1242-46). The state is now the Despotate of Thessalonica; the Nicaean Empire dossier should carry the vassal_start.
1244: Demetrios Angelos Doukas succeeds. 'In 1244, John died and was succeeded by his younger brother' Demetrios, who was unpopular with his subjects.

1246: Nicaea takes Thessalonica. 'Thessalonica was incorporated into the Nicaean state' under the governor Andronikos Palaiologos; Demetrios was exiled to Asia Minor and Theodore to Vodena. The page gives no month (infobox 'Fall of Thessalonica to Nicaea: 1246').

region.text: the state's last land, Thessalonica and its environs

ledger.note: 1246: the Empire of Thessalonica ends. 'Fall of Thessalonica to Nicaea: 1246' (infobox). Cliopatria keeps the row to 1249.

wars.name: Battle of Klokotnitsa
wars.outcome: Theodore's army was destroyed and he was captured; Bulgaria took most of Theodore's Thracian lands and most of Macedonia and Albania; Manuel Komnenos Doukas became Asen's vassal at Thessalonica (1230-37). The lands lost belong to the Epirus dossier's ledger.
wars.note: Listed because it created this state; no zone is drawn for it here.

wars.name: Manuel Komnenos Doukas's recovery of Thessaly

zones.text: Larissa, Pharsalos and several other fortresses

wars.outcome: Manuel, with Nicaean support, takes Larissa and Pharsalos from John in 1239 and rules Thessaly to about 1241; Michael II of Epirus then occupies it.

wars.name: Nicaean takeover of Thessalonica
wars.outcome: Thessalonica is incorporated into the Nicaean state in 1246; Demetrios is exiled to Asia Minor.
wars.note: The page gives no battle or siege; Vatatzes 'wrested much of Thrace as well as most of Macedonia from Bulgaria' in the same year, which does not concern this state's land.

certainty.note: Thirteenth-century frontiers around Thessalonica are known from towns and fortresses, never boundaries; no page delimits the realm.

notes: Written 2026-10-19 by eu-05-e from two pages (budget 1-2). Start 1230, not Cliopatria's 1236 or the infobox's 1224: the despotate-of-epirus dossier records the 1224-1230 state (styled Empire of Thessalonica from 1225/1227) and the 1230 split, so this dossier begins at the split. 1230-1235 is a new keyframe borrowing Cliopatria's 1236 shape. Conflict between the pages: the Empire page says Manuel kept Thessalonica's environs 'and the dynasty's lands in Thessaly and Epirus'; the Manuel page names only Thessalonica and its environs in 1230-1237 and has Thessaly come in 1239 (taken from John). Cliopatria draws Thessaly inside the Empire from 1236. The 1236 shape is kept for 1230-1238 on the state's own page; a gap-filler could open Theodore Komnenos Doukas, Michael II and John Komnenos Doukas to settle who held Thessaly in 1230-1237. 1239-1241: the pages have Manuel ruling Thessaly as a separate lordship (with Nicaean support); Cliopatria keeps Thessaly in this row to 1240 and the despotate-of-epirus dossier records the 1241 gain with this slug as counterpart, whereas the pages say Manuel held it then. A short dossier for 'Manuel Komnenos Doukas (Thessaly)' 1239-1241 is suggested; until then the ledger counterpart is a name. Overlordships for other dossiers: Bulgaria 1230-37 (vassal_start for the second-bulgarian-empire dossier, counterpart empire-of-thessalonica) and Nicaea 1242-46 (nicaean-empire dossier). Cliopatria's 1241 row runs to 1249, three years after the Nicaean takeover. No area appears on either page, so no area comparison was possible. Veroia, Serres, Edessa and Platamon are not on the pages opened.
